claims.text: The site has drawn eleven Wardley maps in its articles, seven in a vault and five in a conference talk.
claims.quote: eleven so far in the articles, seven in a vault, five in a conference talk

claims.text: A Wardley map is a graph with two axes of context: a value chain down the page from a user's need, and evolution across the page.
claims.quote: a Wardley map is a graph with two axes of context

claims.text: Simon Wardley's four stages, genesis, custom built, product and commodity, are the scale on every map on the site.
claims.quote: Simon Wardley's four stages, genesis, custom built, product and commodity, are the scale on every map on this site.

claims.text: The evolution axis is a choice: genesis to commodity is one good answer, and risk, data or governance can each be the axis when they answer the question you have.
claims.quote: The horizontal axis is a scale you choose because it answers the question you have, and genesis to commodity is one good answer, not the only one.

claims.text: In 2022 at the Open Security Summit the owner gave a talk arguing that the mapping habit produces eleven shifts in how you see a problem.
claims.quote: the argument was that the mapping habit produces a set of shifts in how you see a problem, eleven of them in that talk

claims.text: Every dot on every map is a claim that can be wrong; a map you cannot be wrong about is a diagram.
claims.quote: A map you cannot be wrong about is a diagram.

claims.text: A great deal of effort is spent optimising at the wrong altitude, and the vertical axis makes that visible: pick the altitude first, then the dot.
claims.quote: A great deal of effort is spent optimising at the wrong altitude

claims.text: Most build-or-buy arguments are two people drawing the same component in different columns, and the map settles which column it is in.
claims.quote: Most build-or-buy arguments are two people drawing the same component in different columns, and the map settles which column it is in.

claims.text: Does the market exist: a commoditised layer is a hard sell, and a layer where everyone is custom building on top of commodities is a market, because each builder would rather buy.
claims.quote: A layer where everyone is custom building, on top of commodities, is a market: each of those builders would rather buy.

claims.text: The components at the commodity end have names, Apple, Google, Stripe, git, and drawing them puts the people you depend on and could plug into on the same page as your own pieces.
claims.quote: The components at the commodity end have names: Apple, Google, Stripe, git.

claims.text: Every map on the site has a person at the top, as a discipline rather than a convention.
claims.quote: Every map here has a person at the top.

claims.text: The mandate stack maps were the first two on the site drawn as a pair on purpose, from the outside and from the inside, rendered in Mermaid's Wardley syntax.
claims.quote: these were the first two maps on this site that were drawn as a pair on purpose

claims.text: The pay after you read map is the clearest build-or-buy reading: every new thing is on the left and stands on something on the right that already existed.
claims.quote: every new thing is on the left, and every one of them stands on something on the right that already existed

claims.text: The passkey work went from design to product in a day because its shoulders were mature, and the one place it was slow was its one immature dependency.
claims.quote: The passkey work went from a design to a product in a day because the shoulders were mature

claims.text: Three more sets live in vaults: Strategy Maps holds the SG/Send strategy as seven maps published on LinkedIn in May 2026, ThreatModCon 2025 has five walkthroughs, and the Agent Desk vault carries its map.
claims.quote: holds the SG/Send strategy as seven Wardley maps, the ones I published on LinkedIn in May 2026

value.unit: Wardley maps in the Strategy Maps vault

claims.text: Taken apart, every layer of sgit is mature and a hard sell; its market is the custom building happening on top of storage, version control and encryption, which is the vault.
claims.quote: The market for sgit is not the three commodities; it is the custom building that is happening on top of them

claims.text: Agents became a commodity in the last year, which moved RiskMandate's dot right and its opportunity up: agent behaviour is all genesis and custom built now.
claims.quote: The map told us the layer below had commoditised before the invoices did.

claims.text: The two readings differ: for sgit the market is above the product, for RiskMandate the product is at the market and the layer below it just moved.
claims.quote: For sgit the market is above the product; for RiskMandate the product is at the market and the layer below it just moved.

claims.text: The afternoon from Pay after you read is read as a story in eight frames, one release at a time.
claims.quote: These are the eight frames of the afternoon from Pay after you read.

claims.text: The method is seven questions in one picture: where is the user, what is new, what does it stand on, where did the movement happen, where did we walk back, where would somebody else hook in, what is next.
claims.quote: Seven questions, one picture, and a reader who did not know the business now knows what it is.

claims.text: Maps nest: every node on a map is a Wardley map, and the place a dot held on the parent's evolution axis is where the child's anchor sits, because maturity does not change when you look inside.
claims.quote: Zoom into a dot and it becomes the anchor of the next map, and the place it held on the parent's evolution axis is where the child's anchor sits

claims.text: The three-altitude figure goes three levels down, from the business to the vault to the door, and up again to the market the business sits in.
claims.quote: The figure goes three levels down.

claims.text: Which altitude to draw is the first decision, and most of the wrong decisions the owner has seen on maps came from drawing the right map at the wrong altitude.
claims.quote: most of the wrong decisions I have seen on maps were made by drawing the right map at the wrong altitude

claims.text: Two decks, plain pages that print to PDF from the browser: Why I love Wardley maps in twelve slides, and Reading one map with one question per frame.
claims.quote: the explanation, using the maps above as the examples. Twelve slides.

claims.text: As of this release each article's graph also lists its figures with file, URL, caption and kind, so every Wardley map on the site is one query rather than a reading list.
claims.quote: as of this release each graph also lists the article's figures: the file, its URL, the caption, the kind the author gave it

claims.text: The animated maps on the site now have play, pause, step and numbered buttons rather than a loop nobody could stop.
claims.quote: the animated maps on this site now have play, pause, step and numbered buttons rather than a loop nobody could stop

claims.text: Three things are offered to the mapping community: the maps as source, the evolution axis as a choice, and the nested reading, which is either a known practice or an extension worth testing.
claims.quote: the nested reading, maps all the way down with the dot as the next anchor, is either already a well-known practice I have not seen written up or an extension worth testing

claims.text: Positions are judgements: every placement on every map is a claim by the author, not a measurement.
claims.quote: Every placement on every map here is a claim by the author, not a measurement of anything.

claims.text: The eleven shifts are a 2022 list; the shorter list in the article is the one used now and is not the same list.
claims.quote: the list in this article is the shorter one I use now, and it is not the same list

claims.text: The alternative-axis post was not found while writing, so the claim that it exists is from memory and the argument is restated, not cited.
claims.quote: the claim that it exists is from memory and the argument is restated, not cited

claims.text: The two market readings are the site's own and can be wrong in the usual way maps are wrong: the layer moves after the map was drawn.
claims.quote: They are how we read our own maps, and they can be wrong in the usual way maps are wrong

claims.text: The fractal rule is a practice, not a theorem; where the inside of a thing is much more or less mature than the thing, it will be worth breaking.
claims.quote: The fractal rule is a practice, not a theorem.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 12 October 2026; no map was drawn new for it except the three-altitude figure and the collage, and the figure indexing shipped in site v0.7.77.
claims.quote: none was drawn new for this piece except the three-altitude figure and the collage
